﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾. Abu Saʿid Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shuraihi informed us; Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Thaʿlabi informed us; Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Sarakhsi, by dictation, narrated to us; Abu al-Wafa al-Muammal ibn al-Hasan ibn Isa al-Masarjisi informed us; Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Khalid narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Buhayr al-Qadi narrated to us, saying: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd al-Sanʿani say: I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to look upon the conditions of the Resurrection, let him recite: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Tafsir, Surat al-Takwir, 9/252-253, and Imam Ahmad, 2/37. al-Hakim authenticated it, 2/515, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur, 8/426, added its attribution to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

The saying of the Exalted, ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾: Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn ʿAbbas: it became dark. Qatadah, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: its light has gone. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: it was overthrown (ghuwwirat). Mujahid said: it was annihilated (idmahalla). Al-Zajjaj said: it is wrapped up as a turban is wrapped; one says: "I wrapped the turban (kawwartu al-ʿimamah) on my head, I wrap it (ukawwiruha) kurar, and I wrapped it takwiran, when I folded it." The origin of takwir is gathering part of a thing onto part of another, so its meaning is that the sun is gathered part onto part and then wrapped; when that is done to it, its light goes away. [[Ibn Jarir mentioned these sayings, 30/94-95, then said, giving preference: "The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is to say: (kuwwirat) as Allah, may His praise be exalted, said, and takwir in the speech of the Arabs is gathering part of a thing onto part of another, like the wrapping of a turban, which is winding it on the head, and like takwir al-karah, which is gathering garments part onto part and folding them. Likewise His saying (idha al-shamsu kurrat) means: gathering part of it onto part, then wrapping it and casting it away; when this is done to it, its light goes away. So according to the interpretation we have stated and explained, both of the sayings you mentioned from the scholars of interpretation have a sound basis, since when it is wrapped up and cast away, its light goes."]]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: On the Day of Resurrection Allah will wrap the sun, the moon and the stars and cast them into the sea; then He will send upon them a western wind (rih dabur), which will strike them so they become fire. [[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur, 8/426, to Ibn Abi al-Dunya in "al-Ahwal", and to Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh in "al-ʿAzamah".]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us; Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us; Musaddad narrated to us; Abd al-ʿAziz ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us; Abdullah al-Danaj narrated to us; Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The sun and the moon will be wrapped up on the Day of Resurrection." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Bad' al-Khalq, chapter on the description of the sun and the moon, 6/297, and by the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah, 15/115-116.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 81, verses 2–6:**

﴿وَإِذَا النُّجُومُ انْكَدَرَتْ﴾ ﴿And when the stars fall and scatter.﴾ That is, they scatter from the sky and fall to the earth. It is said: *inkadara al-ta'ir* (the bird fell from its nest). Al-Kalbi and 'Ata' said: On that day the sky will rain down stars, and no star will remain without falling.

﴿وَإِذَا الْجِبَالُ سُيِّرَتْ﴾ ﴿And when the mountains are set in motion.﴾ [They are uprooted [[Addition from "B".]]] from the surface of the earth and become scattered dust [[In "B": *munbathan* (scattered).]].

﴿وَإِذَا الْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْ﴾ ﴿And when the pregnant she-camels are abandoned.﴾ These are the pregnant she-camels whose pregnancy has reached ten months. The singular is *'ushara'* (a she-camel in her tenth month of pregnancy). This remains its name until she gives birth, at the completion of a year. They were the most precious property among the Arabs. "*'Uttilat*" means they are left [neglected [[In "B": *humlan* (neglected).]]] without a herdsman, abandoned by their owners, who had been devoted to their tails (i.e., their care). They had no property more beloved to them than these, because of the terrors of the Day of Resurrection that had come upon them.

﴿وَإِذَا الْوُحُوشُ﴾ ﴿And when the wild beasts﴾ — meaning the land animals — ﴿حُشِرَتْ﴾ ﴿are gathered.﴾ They are gathered after the Resurrection, so that retribution may be taken for some of them from others. 'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: Their gathering is their death. He also said: The gathering of every thing is its death, except the jinn and mankind, for they will be made to stand (for judgment) on the Day of Resurrection. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: They became mixed together.

﴿وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ سُجِّرَتْ﴾ ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze.﴾ The people of Makkah and Basra read *sujjirat* with the light (single-consonant) form, while the others read it with the intensive form. Ibn 'Abbas said: They are kindled and become fire blazing up. Mujahid and Muqatil said: It means that some of them are burst into others, the sweet and the salt, so that all the seas become one sea. Al-Kalbi said: They are filled. This also is the meaning of ﴿وَالْبَحْرِ الْمَسْجُورِ﴾ ﴿and by the sea that is filled﴾ [al-Tur: 6], and *al-masjur* means the filled. It was also said: Their waters become one sea of boiling water for the people of the Fire. Al-Hasan said: They dry up, and this is the view of Qatadah, who said: Their water has gone, and not a drop remains in them.

Abu al-'Aliyah narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: Six signs will come before the Day of Resurrection. While people are in their markets, the light of the sun will disappear [, and while they are in that state, the stars will scatter [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "B".]], and while they are in that state, the mountains will fall upon the surface of the earth and will shake and tremble. The jinn will flee to mankind, and mankind to the jinn. The animals, the birds, and the wild beasts will be mixed together, and some of them will surge against others. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا الْوُحُوشُ حُشِرَتْ﴾ ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ [[Omitted from "B": "mixed together".]] ﴿وَإِذَا الْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْ وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ سُجِّرَتْ﴾ ﴿And when the pregnant she-camels are abandoned, and when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: The jinn said to mankind, "We will bring you the news." So they went to the sea, and behold, it was a fire blazing. He said: While they were in that state, the earth split open in one crack down to the lowest seventh earth, and the sky split open in one rupture up to the highest seventh heaven. While they were in that state, a wind came upon them and caused them to die [[Narrated by al-Tabari (30/63–64) as a *mawquf* report from Ubayy. Al-Suyuti cited it in *al-Durr al-Manthur* (8/427) from Ibn Abi al-Dunya in *al-Ahwal* and from Ibn Abi Hatim.]].

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 81, verses 12–19:**

﴿And when Hell is ignited﴾. The people of Medina, the people of Syria, and Hafs from ʿAsim read *"suʿʿirat"* (سُعِّرَتْ) with the doubled ʿayn (tashdid). The rest read it without doubling (takhfif). It means: it is kindled for the enemies of God.

﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾: it is brought near to the friends of God.

﴿Then every soul will know﴾ at that time ﴿what it has brought forth﴾, meaning every soul will know what it has brought forth of good or evil. This is the answer to His saying: "When the sun is wrapped up" and what follows it.

The Exalted and Majestic said: ﴿So I swear by the receding stars﴾. Here *"la"* (لَا) is redundant (zaʾidah), and the meaning is: I swear by the receding ones ﴿that run and hide﴾. Qatadah said: they are the stars that appear at night and recede by day, so they are hidden and not seen.

It is also reported from Ali that they are the planets (kawakib) that recede by day so they are not seen, and that *"takannas"* (تَكْنَسُ) means they retreat and return to their courses.

Some people said: they are the five planets: Saturn (Zuhal), Jupiter (al-Mushtari), Mars (al-Mirrikh), Venus (al-Zuhrah), and Mercury (ʿUtarid). *"Takhnasu"* (تَخْنَسُ) means they move back along their course, that is, they return backward; and *"taknasu"* (تَكْنَسُ) means they conceal themselves at the time of their disappearance and setting, as gazelles hide in their caves.

Ibn Zayd said: the meaning of *"al-khunnas"* (الْخُنَّسِ) is that they recede, that is, they fall behind their risings each year by an amount that they lag behind the earlier rising; they recede from it. And *"al-kunnas"* (الْكُنَّسِ) means they hide by day and are not seen. Al-Aʿmash reported from Ibrahim, from Abdullah, that they are the wild animals (al-wahsh).

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: they are the gazelles. This is also the report of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas.

The root meaning of *khunus* (خُنُوس) is returning backward, and *kunus* (كُنُوس) is seeking shelter in their lairs (*makanis*), which are the places where wild animals take refuge.

﴿And by the night when it turns away﴾. Al-Hasan said: it approaches with its darkness. Others said: it withdraws. The Arabs say: *"ʿasʿasa al-layl"* (عَسْعَسَ اللَّيْلُ) and *"saʿsaʿa"* (سَعْسَعَ), meaning the night has withdrawn and little of it remains.

﴿And by the dawn when it breathes﴾: it approaches and its beginning appears. It was also said: its light extends and rises.

﴿Indeed, it﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿is the word of a noble messenger﴾, meaning Gabriel, that is: Gabriel brought it down from God, Exalted is He.
